title: McAfee Station on the Salt River
summary: The McAfee brothers surveyed Salt River bottomlands in today’s Mercer County in 1773 and built McAfee Station there in 1779, sheltering local families.
bodyMarkdown:
McAfee Station was a pioneer fort on the Salt River in today's Mercer County. It grew out of the surveys of the McAfee Company, a group of Virginia brothers and their partners. The settlement around it helped shape early central Kentucky.

## The 1773 survey

The [McAfee Company](https://explorekyhistory.ky.gov/items/show/987) was made up of the brothers Robert, James Jr. and George McAfee, with James McCoun Jr. and Samuel Adams. They left Virginia on May 10, 1773, drawn by long hunters' stories of the land beyond the mountains. The brothers held a land grant for service in the French and Indian War.

At the mouth of the Kanawha the party joined Thomas Bullitt's surveyors. The groups split at the mouth of the Kentucky River. The McAfees followed Eagle Creek to [Drennon Springs](/stories/drennon-springs-salt-works/) and surveyed land at the future site of Frankfort, but Robert McAfee never entered that survey. They then followed the Salt River, which they called Crooked Creek, into present Mercer County and claimed land there.

## Delays

Their return was held up by Native nations fighting to keep control of their homelands. The brothers also served with General Lewis at the Battle of Point Pleasant. In February 1775 the company set out again, crossed Cumberland Gap and reached James McAfee's spring on March 11. There they found that their surveys overlapped those of James Harrod. Harrod had built cabins and planted corn, so he won the disputed land.

Families prepared to move in 1776. Enslaved people owned by the McAfee and McCoun families were also brought, not by their choice. Low water forced the river party back, and the brothers served again in the Revolutionary War in 1777 and 1778.

## The station

The company returned in 1779 and reached the Harrodsburg land office on September 27. The KHS marker text says a stockade was built that year on James McAfee's land on the Salt River by the McAfee, McCoun, McGee, Curry and Adams families. As conflict with the Shawnee grew, nearly every family in the area lived at the station by 1781.

On May 9, probably in 1781, a Shawnee war party attacked the station. With the riflemen running low on ammunition, the nearby William McAfee Station sent runners to Fort Harrod and McGary's Station. A small armed party arrived and drove off the attack.

After [George Rogers Clark's](/stories/george-rogers-clark/) 1780 campaign against Shawnee towns in Ohio, many Shawnee and other Native people [left Kentucky](https://explorekyhistory.ky.gov/items/show/987). By 1783 several families had moved onto their own land.

## Kentucky today

The marker records that New Providence Presbyterian Church was formed in 1785. The third church built by that congregation still stands nearby. The marker also honors John May, who taught the station's first school in 1779. The station is now part of [an unincorporated community in Mercer County](https://explorekyhistory.ky.gov/items/show/987).

[Ann McGinty](/stories/ann-mcginty-and-kentuckys-first-spinning-wheel/) of Harrodsburg [solved the problem of making cloth on the frontier](https://explorekyhistory.ky.gov/items/show/987).
